title: Count Mirror Slices
statement:
Given a string s, count its non-empty contiguous slices that read the same forwards and backwards.

Slices at different positions count separately, even when they spell the same text.

examples.why: The four single letters, "bb" and "abba". Only letter-centred counting would miss the two even-length ones.
All 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 slices are mirrors. Counting distinct texts would give only 4.
7 single letters, then "cec", "aceca" and "racecar", all grown from the same centre e.

hints: Every mirror slice has a centre: a letter or the gap between two letters.
From a centre, each step outward that still matches gives exactly one more mirror slice. So the count from one centre is the number of successful steps.
Expand from all 2n − 1 centres and add one per matching step. Or fill mir[i][j] = s[i] == s[j] && mir[i+1][j−1] and count the trues.

explain.intuition:
This is the counting twin of finding the longest mirror slice. State: mir[i][j] = s[i..j] reads the same both ways. Recurrence: mir[i][j] = s[i] == s[j] && (j − i < 2 || mir[i+1][j−1]), filled by increasing length. The answer is the number of true cells.

Look at that recurrence from the inside out and the table disappears. Each mirror is its centre plus some matching pairs around it, so it is found by expanding from its centre. Every successful expansion step is one new mirror. Summing over all 2n − 1 centres counts each mirror exactly once, because each slice has exactly one centre.
steps: State (table version): mir[i][j] = true when s[i..j] is a mirror; mir[i][j] = s[i] == s[j] && (j − i < 2 || mir[i+1][j−1]).
Centre version: for each centre (c, c) and (c, c + 1), set lo, hi to it.
While lo ≥ 0, hi < n and s[lo] == s[hi]: add 1 to the count, then widen.
pitfalls: Skipping the between-letter centres. "abba" then counts 4 instead of 6.
Collecting the mirrors in a set of strings. That counts distinct text, and "zzzz" gives 4 instead of 10.
Filling the table row by row from the top. mir[i][j] needs mir[i+1][j−1], which is not ready yet; fill by length, or with i going down.

solutions.title: Check every slice
solutions.idea: Test each of the n(n + 1)/2 slices by comparing it with its reverse.

solutions.title: Table of mirror slices
solutions.idea: Fill mir[i][j] by increasing length from the recurrence and count the true cells.

solutions.title: Expand around every centre
solutions.idea: From each of the 2n − 1 centres, count the matching expansion steps.

followups: Count only mirror slices of length at least 3.
Count the distinct mirror texts instead. How many can a string of length n have at most?
